questions.question: Rina has written 3 quizzes so far, and her three marks add up to 261 points. She wants her mean over all 4 quizzes to be 88. If x stands for her mark on the fourth quiz, which plan finds x?
options: (261 + x) ÷ 3 = 88, then solve that for x
261 + x = 88 × 3, then solve that for x
x = 88, because 88 is the target mean
questions.explain: A mean of 88 over 4 quizzes means all four marks must total 88 × 4 = 352, so (261 + x) ÷ 4 = 88 and x = 91. Dividing by 3 forgets that the new quiz is counted too.

questions.question: A student has 4 quiz marks that add up to 302 points. After one more quiz, the student wants the mean of all 5 quizzes to be 78. What must the 5 quiz marks add up to?
questions.explain: The mean of 78 counts all 5 quizzes, so the total needed is 78 × 5 = 390. Using 78 × 4 = 312 counts only the quizzes already written and leaves the new one out.

questions.question: Over her first 4 swim practices, Ava swam a total of 40 laps. She wants a mean of 12 laps over 5 practices. How many laps must she swim at the fifth practice?
questions.explain: Five practices with a mean of 12 need 12 × 5 = 60 laps altogether, and 60 - 40 = 20 laps at the last practice. Swimming only 12 laps leaves the mean below 12, because the first four practices averaged just 10.

questions.question: Devon has 3 test marks that total 264 points. He wants a mean of 90 once his fourth test is added. Which first step is correct?
options: Divide 264 by 3 to find the needed total
Use 90 as the next mark, since 90 is the goal
Multiply 90 by 3, since 3 tests are written
Multiply 90 by 4 to find the needed total
questions.explain: Start from the total all four tests must reach: 90 × 4 = 360, then subtract 264 to get 96 on the fourth test. Multiplying 90 by 3 leaves the new test out of the count.

questions.question: Priya's first four socials marks are 72%, 85%, 90% and 81%. She wants a mean of 84% after her fifth mark. What must the fifth mark be?
questions.explain: Five marks with a mean of 84 need a total of 84 × 5 = 420, and her four marks give 328, so 420 - 328 = 92. Answering 84 treats the target as the next mark, but her first four marks average only 82, so she must make up that shortfall.

questions.question: Marcus earned $18, $22, $15 and $21 dog-walking on four days. He wants his earnings to have a mean of $20 per day over five days. How much must he earn on day 5?
questions.explain: A mean of $20 over 5 days needs $20 × 5 = $100 in total, and he has $76, so day 5 must bring $24. Earning $20 on day 5 would leave the mean at only $19.20.

questions.question: Leah has 5 quiz marks with a mean of 76. She writes a sixth quiz and wants the mean of all 6 marks to be 78. Which plan finds the mark she needs?
options: Use 78 itself, as 78 is the average she wants
76 × 5 ÷ 6, as the old total is shared over 6
questions.explain: Six marks averaging 78 need 78 × 6 = 468 points, and the five marks so far give 76 × 5 = 380, so the sixth mark must be 88. Multiplying the target by 5 counts only the quizzes already written.

questions.question: In her first 3 basketball games Nadia scored a mean of 12.5 points. She wants a mean of 14 points over 4 games. How many points does she need in game 4?
questions.explain: Three games at 12.5 give 37.5 points, four games at 14 need 56 points, so game 4 needs 56 - 37.5 = 18.5. Scoring just 14 would leave the mean at 12.875, still short of the target.

questions.question: Tomas has four science marks: 68, 74, 80 and 78. Two tests are left, and he wants a mean of 76 over all six marks. He scores 82 on the fifth test. What must he score on the sixth test?
questions.explain: Six marks averaging 76 need 456 points; the first four give 300 and the fifth adds 82, so 456 - 382 = 74 is left for the last test. Splitting the missing 156 points evenly over two tests ignores the 82 he has already banked.

questions.question: Ella has three quiz marks that total 231 points. She wants a mean of 80 over four quizzes and says she just needs 80 on the fourth quiz. What mark does she actually need?
options: 80, because the target mean is the next mark
77, because 231 ÷ 3 = 77 is her mean so far
questions.explain: All four marks must total 80 × 4 = 320, and she has 231, so the fourth mark must be 89. The target mean is what the four marks average out to, not what the next one has to be.

questions.question: Kai saved a mean of $16 per week from his paper route for 5 weeks. He wants a mean of $18 per week over 8 weeks. He saves $21 in week 6 and $19 in week 7. How much must he save in week 8?
questions.explain: Eight weeks at a mean of $18 need $144 in total; he has $80 + $21 + $19 = $120, so week 8 needs $24. Multiplying $18 by 7 weeks, or by only the last 3 weeks, uses the wrong number of weeks.

questions.question: Owen's first four socials tests, each out of 100, are 62, 70, 66 and 72. He wants a mean of 80 after his fifth test. Which statement is true?
options: It is possible if he scores 80, as 80 is his target
It is possible with 100, as 100 is the top mark
It is possible if he scores 50, as 80 × 4 = 320
questions.explain: Five tests averaging 80 need 400 points and he has 270, so he would need 130 on a test worth 100, which cannot happen. Multiplying 80 by 4 instead of 5 makes it look as though 50 would be enough.
